editorial.headline: Air and Space Transport Services Beyond the Usual Categories
editorial.standfirst: Open to every listed business scale and up to 100% foreign ownership nationally, this air-and-space transport activity is not blocked by Bali’s moratorium, subject to address verification.
editorial.body:
“Other” should not be mistaken for vague. This activity covers services connected to air and space transport for passengers, animals or goods when those activities are not classified elsewhere. Its breadth comes from the transport subjects—people, live animals and cargo—and from the fact that it reaches both air and space transport. The practical reading must remain disciplined: the record defines the field by its connection to transport and by what has not been classified elsewhere; it does not offer a neat menu of named services. A registration should therefore be read against that boundary, rather than expanded with examples the classification does not supply.

The scale position is notably broad. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar businesses, so the classification is not reserved for one stated size of enterprise. That does not turn the four scale labels into a description of operational complexity or a set of further conditions; the record supplies only the eligibility range. It does, however, establish a clear starting point for founders: this is an activity available across the full Micro-to-Large sequence recorded here, provided the business genuinely sits within the stated air-and-space transport-related scope.

Nationally, the PMA position is open, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the national record permits full foreign ownership for PMA registration of this activity. The stated source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That national openness is the relevant baseline, but it is not a reason to flatten the local reading. Bali has a separate status and a separate reason, and those fields matter because a national ownership ceiling and a provincial registration position can be different things.

For Bali, the record’s status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. More importantly, it describes the activity as medium-high/high risk and says it is not blocked by the provincial moratorium, with verification required for the address. The moratorium itself is recorded as permanent and island-wide, but this activity is expressly outside its block. So the honest Bali conclusion is narrow but useful: PMA registration is not barred by that moratorium today; the actual address still needs verification. That is neither a new ownership cap nor a condition invented around the activity—it is the specific local qualification the record gives.
